title: Will Wade, LSU players won't attend SEC Basketball Media Day due to 'inclement weather' - CBS Sports
description: SEC Media Day from Birmingham begins on Tuesday, but LSU will not be in attendance
body:
SEC Media Day from Birmingham begins on Tuesday, but LSU will not be in attendance
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:12 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When SEC Media Day begins on Tuesday in Birmingham, Alabama there will be a noticeable absence. LSU coach Will Wade, Kansas State transfer Abdi Bashir Jr. and Kentucky transfer Mouhamed Dioubate won't be in attendance due to "inclement weather," the SEC announced. There was a ground stop in Baton Rouge due to fog on Tuesday morning.Wade was scheduled to speak second at the event, after Auburn coach Steven Pearl and players Kevin Overton and Tahaad Pettiford took questions from reporters. LSU women's coach Kim Mulkey was also scheduled to appear at SEC Media Day on Tuesday alongside MiLaysia Fulwiley, ZaKiyah Johnson and Mikaylah Williams, but they will also not be in attendance.
The Tigers were picked to finish 14th in the preseason SEC poll release on Monday, with Mississippi State and South Carolina being the only teams selected to finish below them. LSU fired Matt McMahon after four seasons with the program after the Tigers finished last (3-15) in the SEC last season.Wade's roster construction has been under a microscope this season, due to a handful of his players currently in eligibility limbo. LSU had its exhibition debut last week against McNeese and came away with a 63-60 win despite playing just seven players. The Tigers had just four players listed on their active roster as of a few days ago, before it was updated to include 10 total players.
Notable additions to LSU's roster over the last few days include UCLA transfer Donovan Dent, international big man Michael Ružić and freshman Jordan Bender. Notable players Wade recruited this offseason that still aren't listed on the team's official roster: Former Big East Player of the Year RJ Luis Jr., UCLA transfer Skyy Clark and Gilad Levy, Brice Dessert and Saliou Niang from the international ranks.
        
            
                SEC basketball 2026-27 preseason poll and predictions: Alabama, Georgia overrated; LSU, Missouri underrated
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Wade has made a handful of media appearances in recent weeks, including his first public remarks about his "unconventional" roster last month, ahead of his team's first scrimmage against McNeese."What we're doing is unconventional," Wade said last month. "I understand that. But, 20 years ago, Airbnb was unconventional. Everybody stayed in a hotel. Fifteen years ago, you rode in a taxi everywhere. Now you take Uber. So, like, just because it's unconventional doesn't mean it's not going to work. Now, it may not work. If it doesn't work, write about what an idiot I am. I understand that. But just because it's unconventional, like I told our guys, we're going to be unconventional. We're going to be unapologetic about it. It is what it is. We're going to be unapologetic. This is who we are. This is what we're doing. This is the path that we charted. We're going to go down it."
LSU has two scrimmages left against UCF (on Wednesday) and Florida State (Oct. 24) before it opens the 2026-27 campaign at home against New Orleans on Nov. 3

title: Five NFL teams getting the most out of their rookie class: Dolphins, Browns leading the way - CBS Sports
description: Miami is on a near-record pace with 14 first-year contributors, while the Ravens and the Chargers also lean heavi
body:
Miami is on a near-record pace with 14 first-year contributors, while the Ravens and the Chargers also lean heavily on newcomers
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:05 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Week 5 of the NFL season has come and gone, and we have a good sample size of snaps so far, including from rookies. Seven teams had more than one pick in the first round of the 2026 draft: Jets, Browns, Titans, Chiefs, Giants, Cowboys and Dolphins. So, how are those rookie classes performing in relation to others? There are several ways to measure and weigh the impact of rookie performers, but there is no substitute for playing time. Before getting into the teams whose rookies have played the most, the five lowest snap totals belong to the Broncos (63), Rams (194), Seahawks (283), Eagles (403) and Cardinals (545). Here are the rookie classes that have played the most snaps this season: 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Baltimore Ravens: 1,101 snapsBaltimore's rookie class is headlined by offensive lineman Vega Ioane. He was playing right guard but was forced to start at center in Week 5, and the acquisition of Cam Jurgens will allow the Ravens to get the five best linemen on the field. Ioane is allowing pressure for every 32.4 pass blocking snaps, according to TruMedia. Rookie tight ends Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas have helped the franchise absorb the losses of Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar. Wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane saw a significant workload in Week 1, but was then lost for the season due to injury. 
Cornerback Chandler Rivers and edge rushers Zion Young and Ethan Burke have also factored into the defensive rotation. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. New York Giants: 1,246 snapsNew York made two selections in the top-10 overall: linebacker Arvell Reese and right guard Francis Mauigoa. Those two players have accounted for more than half of the Giants' rookie snap counts. Additionally, 22% of the rookie snap count has been played on special teams. Reese has looked the part through five games. Mauigoa is allowing a pressure once every 18.7 pass blocking snaps, according to TruMedia. Cornerback Colton Hood has started two games for the team. Wide receiver Malachi Fields has been an asset in both the run and the pass. I wrote about Fields as one of the non-first-round picks who have taken on a large role this season. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Los Angeles Chargers: 1,301 snapsLos Angeles is off to an unforeseen and uncharacteristic 0-5 start. The team's issues go well beyond injuries, but those, too, have taken a toll. When veteran center Tyler Biadasz suffered a season-ending injury prior to the season, it forced Day 2 selection Jake Slaughter into the starting lineup. Slaughter is allowing a pressure for every 25.7 pass blocking snaps, according to TruMedia. Ten rookies have taken offensive or defensive snaps for the Chargers this season. Of the 612 offensive snaps, five offensive linemen have combined for all but 22. Safety Genesis Smith and edge rusher Akheem Mesidor are fully immersed in the defensive rotation. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Cleveland Browns: 1,401 snapsAll of Cleveland's top-100 overall selections have delivered thus far. Spencer Fano and Austin Barber are starting at left tackle and right guard, respectively. Fano is allowing a pressure for every 23.1 pass blocking snaps, according to TruMedia. Barber is allowing a pressure for every 46.3 pass blocking snaps. Wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion rank in the top three on the team in each of the following receiving categories: receptions, yards and targets. Safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has seen his role expand with each passing week. His length and aggressiveness playing downhill have allowed the team to be more creative with personnel and blitz packages. McNeil-Warren often takes on the role of playing single high when the team opts for it. 
Cleveland's five other draft selections have a combined 118 snaps; all but three of which have come on special teams. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Miami Dolphins: 2,090 snapsMiami is on pace for 7,106 rookie snaps played this season, which is just off the pace for the most played in a season over the last decade. The Browns' 2016 rookie class played 7,185 snaps during a 16-game season. I previously wrote about that Browns class and other high-volume rookie classes over the last decade. Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez leads all NFL players with 57 tackles. He, along with safety Michael Taaffe, cornerback Chris Johnson, and offensive guard Kadyn Proctor, has played 250+ snaps this season. Proctor is allowing a pressure for every 22.9 pass blocking snaps, per TruMedia. 
Some of that is born out of necessity, as Miami has arguably the most talent-deficient roster in the league. It is one of three winless teams this season, after all. Contributions go well beyond the team's first and second round picks, however. In addition to Taaffe, Miami has leaned heavily on rookie wide receivers Chris Bell, Kevin Coleman Jr. and Caleb Douglas, the latter of whom has missed time dealing with an injury. In total, the team has played 14 rookies this season.

title: Arizona Cardinals QB situation: Why it's time for Carson Beck to replace Jacoby Brissett - CBS Sports
description: A look at the Cardinals' quarterback outlook and when Carson Beck should start
body:
A look at the Cardinals' quarterback outlook and when Carson Beck should start
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:20 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Arizona Cardinals (1-4) have hit their ceiling with Jacoby Brissett as their starting quarterback in 2026. Since defeating the now 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, Arizona has lost four in a row, including a damning couple of losses the last two weeks. The Cardinals had a chance to beat the New York Giants in Week 4 with a play at the 4-yard line, trailing by six with 11 seconds remaining. After using their final timeout, Brissett threw a pick-six, the third of his single-game career-high three interceptions that day. Equally — or perhaps more — damning is what happened on Sunday in Arizona's 45-21 defeat against the Detroit Lions. The Lions entered Week 5 with the league's 31st-ranked scoring defense (31.8 points per game) and the NFL's worst total defense (423.8 total yards per game) and third down defense (52.8% third down conversion rate allowed). After an opening drive touchdown pass from Brissett to tight end Teagan Quitoriano, the Cardinals' next five drives were three-and-outs. That's right. Arizona had five consecutive three-and-outs against the league's worst total and third-down defense. Their next drive ended with an interception. It wasn't until the game was essentially over that Brissett found the end zone again.That leaves the question: Is it time for Carson Beck to take over in Arizona?A closer look at BrissettEvery quarterback who had played the Lions entering Week 5 stuffed the stat sheet and either beat Detroit or lost to them by one possession. The Brissett-led Cardinals losing to the 2026 Lions defense, which is missing both All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph and Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch, by 24 points is unacceptable. 
Quarterbacks vs. the Lions this seasonNew Orleans Saints' Tyler Shough (Week 1): 35-for-56 for 410 yards passing, three passing touchdowns, two interceptions in a 31-30 OT lossBuffalo Bills' Josh Allen (Week 2): 20-for-31 for 248 yards passing, three passing touchdowns; 14 carries for 69 yards, two rushing touchdowns in a 41-31 winNew York Jets' Geno Smith (Week 3): 31-for-37 for 321 yards passing, three passing touchdowns in a 31-24 lossCarolina Panthers' Bryce Young (Week 4): 29-for-41 for 329 yards passing, two passing touchdowns in a 32-26 win 
Brissett's production this season — 66.3% completion percentage, 1,110 yards passing, nine passing touchdowns and five interceptions for an 85.2 passer rating — isn't terrible, but it's all empty calories in that it mostly happens with the game's outcome no longer up in the air. The 2026 season isn't an outlier for Brissett either. In 2025, he threw for 3,366 passing yards, the second most in the NFL since becoming a starter in Week 6, but they weren't impactful. Arizona won just one of Brissett's 11 starts in 2025, and it was against the Dallas Cowboys, who owned that season's worst scoring defense (30.1 points allowed per game). Brissett is what he is: a 33-year-old journeyman on his sixth NFL team in 11 seasons who is limited as a full-time starting quarterback. Should it be rookie Carson Beck's time?A strong case could be made that 2026 third-round pick Carson Beck should begin to receive increased reps in practice before eventually replacing Brissett in the starting lineup. Beck played just one preseason game, the Hall of Fame game against the Carolina Panthers, but he performed well. He threw for 188 yards and a touchdown while completing 15 of his 19 throws. 
A rib injury cut short his development opportunities as he missed the final three Cardinals preseason games. Thus far this season, he has been the emergency third quarterback on game day. "If we think that's what's best," said Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur on Monday when asked about moving Beck to an active role. "We haven't had those discussions. We'll end up having that discussion [Tuesday]."   Sure, a one-game preseason sample size isn't incredibly indicative of a quarterback's long-term NFL potential, but it's worth ramping Beck up to start. The next two weeks are against difficult defenses in the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos, but Arizona should target Week 8 for Beck to make his regular-season debut. 
Why Week 8? That's when the Cardinals will head to AT&T Stadium to face the Dallas Cowboys (2-3), the only team Brissett beat in 2025 and the owners of the NFL's current seventh-worst scoring defense (27.2 points per game allowed in 2026). The Cowboys are fresh off an embarrassing loss to the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who earned their first win of 2026 with undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels making his second career start.Arizona needs to get Beck, an older rookie who will turn 25 years old in November, reps for at least the second half of this season. It'll only help to assess what the Cardinals have in him ahead of utilizing another high draft pick in the vaunted 2027 NFL Draft. If they like what they see, the Cardinals can simply go with the "best player available" approach. If they don't, they may need to take a longer look at the upcoming quarterback draft class.

body:
Despite its win over Oregon over the weekend, the Bruins find themselves on the outside looking in entering Week 7, while Notre Dame rose two spots ahead of its clash at BYU
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:52 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        UCLA is riding high off a road win over Oregon and its first 5-0 start since 2022.First-year coach Bob Chesney has injected new energy into the Bruins that has the college football world talking. The preseason expectations, which might have been as simple as making a bowl, have already been significantly heightened. Midway through the season, UCLA now has the 14th-best playoff odds in the country, according to CBS Sports' forecasting and projections team. With an easy schedule that includes only one ranked opponent (No. 19 USC) remaining, one could easily talk themselves into UCLA being this year's version of that 2024 Indiana team. And then disaster struck when veteran quarterback Nico Iamaleava went down with a significant knee injury against the Ducks. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reported Monday that Iamaleava is expected to miss the rest of the season. 
If you haven't watched UCLA at all this season, the loss of Iamaleava is significant. The former five-star recruit had elevated his play under Chesney and was positioning himself to possibly be a Day 2 NFL Draft pick next year. Before the injury, Iamaleava had thrown for 982 passing yards and four touchdowns. Iamaleava's injury is the reason you won't see UCLA listed in our College Football Playoff bracket projections below. Cal Poly transfer quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who has thrown six passes for the Bruins this season, has massive shoes to fill. Getting a resurgent Wisconsin team in his first start for the Bruins isn't an easy task, either.If there's a silver lining from a playoff committee standpoint, the injury occurred early enough in the season that, should UCLA continue to win at a high rate, it shouldn't be penalized for it. Florida State was famously left out of the 2023 four-team playoff after starting quarterback Jordan Travis suffered a season-ending injury in the second-to-last week of the regular season. FSU didn't have enough time to prove it was just as capable without Travis -- if it could ever do so in the committee's eyes -- and was left out in favor of Alabama.
That shouldn't be the case for UCLA. Dieffenbach and the Bruins have upcoming chances against Wisconsin, Michigan State, Minnesota, Michigan and USC to prove they are playoff-worthy. With the nation's No. 6 rushing offense (253 yards per game) and a talented defense that forced a whopping seven turnovers against Oregon, UCLA doesn't need huge numbers out of its new quarterback. Even average QB play that can help prevent opposing defenses from stacking the box against star running back Wayne Knight would be hugely beneficial. If UCLA goes undefeated, it will be in the playoff field. If it goes 11-1 and Oregon doesn't completely collapse, it'll have a strong argument to be in the field. A 10-2 finish with losses to Wisconsin and USC could be enough to keep it out. If UCLA wins this weekend, its playoff odds would improve to 36.4%. Beyond simply the final score, though, the attention will be on how UCLA looks without Iamaleava. 

        
            
                CBS Sports 138: Georgia takes top spot over Miami, Notre Dame in college football rankings
                
                    Chip Patterson                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 Georgia 6-0 (SEC champion)The Bulldogs finally take their rightful spot atop these projections. I had wanted to move Georgia up earlier, as my preseason SEC champion pick, but gave Texas the benefit of the doubt after its early resume-entrenching win over Ohio State. No longer. Georgia is the best team in the country and is essentially a mathematical lock (99.8%) to make the playoff, according to our forecasting model. The Bulldogs have a real shot to go undefeated this season at this rate, though there are still challenging games like Ole Miss, Missouri and Florida left. Previous: 3
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Ohio State 5-1 (Big Ten champion)The Buckeyes have remained at the No. 2 spot for most of this season, and nothing has happened to change that. Ohio State made it look easy in a 45-16 home win over Maryland. Leaving Ohio State here is essentially baking in a win over Indiana this weekend in a top-five showdown. A win Saturday would give OSU nearly 90% odds to make the field. Previous: 2
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 3 Miami 5-0 (ACC champion)The Hurricanes are sitting pretty atop the ACC coming out of a bye week. Next up is a struggling Florida State team that could really use a win to improve Mike Norvell's job security. Previous: 3

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 Notre Dame 6-0The Fighting Irish absolutely clobbered Stanford, 58-7, in one of the most impressive results of the season. Notre Dame totaled five rushing touchdowns and 361 rushing yards while making Stanford look like an FCS opponent. That should bode well headed into its toughest test of the year thus far at BYU this weekend. If Notre Dame can win, the model loves its odds of making the field (98%). Previous: 6
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 Alabama 5-1Even with a loss, Alabama doesn't drop in our projections. The Crimson Tide very much looked the part in a close 20-17 loss to Georgia, which featured a few controversial calls against Alabama. Keelon Russell looks like the real deal, and the schedule looks plenty manageable down the stretch, especially if the Tide can get past Tennessee in Knoxville this weekend. With a win over the Vols, Alabama's playoff odds would improve to 87.7%. Previous: 5
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 Indiana 6-0The Hoosiers escaped with a comeback road win over Nebraska that both showed their resiliency and exposed some weaknesses. Curt Cignetti told me before the season they'd run the ball more than Josh Hoover experienced at TCU to take some pressure off him. That approach largely worked before Nebraska, where the Hoosiers managed only 65 rushing yards. There are still some questions around Hoover's consistency and accuracy, which could become factors Saturday against Ohio State. Previous: 7

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 Texas 4-1The wobbly Longhorns finally toppled over in a last-second loss to Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry. Texas had the best win in the country (Ohio State) but had rarely looked like the actual best team in the country. The loss cranked up the questions around Steve Sarkisian as the play-caller, Arch Manning as the quarterback and others associated with a Texas team that looks off. The Longhorns have a big opportunity to quiet the critics against a suddenly desperate Florida team coming off consecutive blowout losses. Previous: 1
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 Texas Tech 5-0 (Big 12 champion)The Red Raiders stay at No. 8 following a bye week. Next up is an Arizona State team that hasn't been great but feels like the kind of tricky game that will be close late. Texas Tech has remained the Big 12 champion pick because it has the easiest remaining schedule of the primary contenders. Previous: 8
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 Ole Miss 4-1The Rebels looked great in a blowout 52-17 road win over Vanderbilt. The tougher test comes this weekend against a 5-1 Missouri team that might be the positive surprise of the early SEC season. A loss to Missouri would be devastating for Ole Miss' playoff hopes, dropping the Rebels' odds to 6.8%. A big reason why: Ole Miss still has Texas, Georgia and Mississippi State left on the schedule. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 10 Utah 5-0The Utes have the seventh-best playoff odds in the country (72.3%) and are well-positioned to make the field especially if they can beat BYU on Nov. 7. A hapless Colorado team should be no problem for Utah this weekend. Utah moved up one spot with Oregon dropping out of the projected field. Previous: 11
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 11 Kentucky 5-1The Wildcats jumped into our projections for the first time after an overtime win over LSU. First-year coach Will Stein is your early frontrunner for Coach of the Year for what he's already done with a program that went 5-7 a season ago. The CBS forecasting model is still skeptical of Kentucky's chances (only 9.2% odds currently), but a win over Oklahoma in what screams a potential letdown game would boost those odds to 19%. Previous: NR
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 12 Boise State 5-1Boise State successfully handled one of its toughest remaining challenges Saturday in a 38-28 win over Fresno State. Boise State's remaining five regular-season opponents have a combined 11-15 record so far. If Boise State can get past Oregon State on Nov. 14, the Broncos could be playoff-bound. Previous: 12

title: Georgia's KJ Bolden admits Bulldogs got away with pass interference vs. Alabama - CBS Sports
description: The no-call late in the fourth quarter helped Georgia close out Alabama on the road
body:
The no-call late in the fourth quarter helped Georgia close out Alabama on the road
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:43 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Georgia's 20-17 win at Alabama over the weekend featured several controversial plays, few bigger than a no-call on the Crimson Tide's final possession, which led to fans throwing objects onto the field after the game.Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell heaved one in the direction of Rico Scott in single coverage for a potential touchdown before Georgia's KJ Bolden came over from his safety spot and broke up the play -- by getting to Scott earlier.Replay showed Bolden and Georgia defensive back Braylon Conley make contact with Scott before the pass came down, which prevented him from making the catch. Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer lost his mind on the sideline, taking off his hat and stomping before arguing for a call."I'm not going to lie, if they did that to us, I'd want them to call pass interference," Bolden told ABC-Atlanta this week.
Russell was sacked by Georgia on the next play, ending any shot at a scoring threat."We can't put the game in the situation where the officials come into play," DeBoer said after the game. "We got to control the things we control."Earlier in the contest, Bolden went headfirst into Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams to dislodge a potential reception on third down. Targeting was not called on the play despite Coleman-Williams, and now, Alabama's top wideout is unlikely to play this weekend at Tennessee, according to coach Kalen DeBoer.
After the no-call on Bolden on the pass intended for Scott in the end zone, Alabama still had all three timeouts and the two-minute timeout to get the ball back, but never did. Ironically, it was a penalty that sealed the Crimson Tide's fate, as Dijon Lee Jr. was whistled for unsportsmanlike conduct while jawing back and forth with a Georgia player after a play on the ensuing possession.Alabama's statement on fan conductAngered by the second-half officiating, Crimson Tide fans threw objects onto the field after the game, prompting Georgia staffers to enforce helmet use for players walking to the locker room.
Losing to a rival in a nationally ranked showdown is one thing, but the multiple disputed no-calls spiked the temperature."Alabama takes matters of fan conduct seriously and expects everyone at our events to demonstrate respect to the student-athletes, coaches, staff, officials and visitors," the school said in a statement to USA Today. "Such conduct will not be tolerated."

title: Fantasy Football Week 6 risers and fallers: Jordan Love moves into must-start territory - CBS Sports
description: Jordan Love and Drake Maye climb the Week 6 Fantasy projections, while RJ Harvey and Rome Odunze lose ground amid
body:
Jordan Love and Drake Maye climb the Week 6 Fantasy projections, while RJ Harvey and Rome Odunze lose ground amid shifting roles
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:58 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While last week was our introduction to the byes, it was a soft launch with just two teams on a bye. This week, we won't have the Lions, Bengals, Vikings or Dolphins. Oh, my. It's even a little worse than that sounds. While the Lions' offense is arguably the best in football, their defense has been a free space for us to attack all season. The net result, unsurprisingly, is that projected scores are down for Week 6 and the bar is much lower to be a starting option, especially at running back. If you are looking for a bright side, we are projecting Caleb Williams, Rashee Rice, and Jalen Coker to return from their injuries. Needless to say, they are all starting options this week. One thing to keep in mind for this week is that with all these good players hurt or on bye, there are going to be some very uncomfortable waivers decisions. Managers, maybe even you, are going to have to drop someone they don't want to just so they can fill out a starting lineup. If you aren't somebody scrambling for starters, keep your eye on the transactions report after waivers run. I expect to see some of our favorite stashes dropped for bye week or injury replacements. Prominent players, we had projected last week that we are not projecting to play in Week 6 as of Monday evening: Quinshon Judkins (and his backup Raheim Sanders), David Montgomery, TreVeyon Henderson, Will Shipley, Deebo Samuel, Tre Harris, Roman Wilson, KC Concepcion, T.J. Hockenson, Kenyon Sadiq
At the bottom of this article are my Week 6 projections for quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and tight end. They will be updated throughout the week as we get more information. Risers Jordan Love, QB, Packers
This is not just a reaction to Love throwing for 367 yards and two touchdowns against the Bears on Sunday. It is partially a reaction to the fact that Love has thrown for 1,408 yards and 10 touchdowns in five games and has multiple touchdown passes in every game. The Packers simply cannot run the football and both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are on fire. But this is mostly about a great matchup against the Cowboys. Every QB they have faced except for Jalon Daniels has scored at least 25 points against them and the Packers have an inflated implied total of 27.5 points as a result of Dallas' defensive ineptitude. Unless you have Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford, or Brock Purdy, you should be starting Love this week.Drake Maye, QB, Patriots
Maye has been in this column three weeks in a row, the last two in the risers section. He's gone from someone we don't want to start at all, to someone we are maybe okay with, to someone who is a must-start QB once again. The Jets may provide a slightly more difficult matchup than the Raiders, but they are not a defense to run away from. 
Dameon Pierce, RB, Eagles
This is lining up to be one of the biggest waiver wire roulettes of the season. If Saquon Barkley and Will Shipley are both out, then Pierce projects as a top 20 running back with 18 touches. If Shipley comes back, Pierce may still be a good flex. If Barkley comes back, Pierce may not be worth anything at all. Pay close attention to the news coming out of Philadelphia, but if the situation remains murky and you are desperate for a running back, Pierce is going to be the biggest swing you can take. This is also probably the biggest swing in run defense faced week over week. Last week, Philadelphia faced a Jacksonville defense that has allowed a league-best 2.53 yards per carry to running backs. This week, they face a Carolina defense that gives up a league-worst 5.39 yards per carry to backs.Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots
Without TreVeyon Henderson, there is a decent chance Stevenson sees 20 touches in Week 6. I have him projected for 18 touches, which gets him into the top 15 in all formats. Stevenson's rushing efficiency has been hit or miss this year, but he has at least three catches in four of his five games. The Jets have given up five touchdowns to running backs in their last three games and have allowed backs to average 4.4 catches per game against them.Woody Marks, RB, Texans
Much like Stevenson, Marks should be in line for a larger workload without David Montgomery. Marks has been the Texans' best rusher this season and he is dangerous in the passing game as well. While this is never going to be an efficient rushing attack, they may have more success this weekend against a Colts defense that has surrendered 4.7 yards per carry to running backs. That is the sixth-worst mark in the league.
Malik Nabers, WR, Giants
Like Maye, Nabers is on the rise for a second week in a row. Jameis Winston is playing better football and the Giants have played two of the worst pass defenses in the NFL. The Saints aren't as bad as the Cardinals and Commanders, but they haven't been very good either. Most importantly, the Saints should score enough points to keep the Giants in a pass-heavy script. Germie Bernard, WR, Steelers
Michael Pittman is on Injured Reserve and Roman Wilson is expected to miss a few weeks. Bernard saw nine targets and scored 14 PPR points without a touchdown in Week 5. Aaron Rodgers is throwing 36.8 passes per game, so there is plenty of volume to go around for Bernard and his teammates. Speaking of...Pat Freiermuth, TE, Steelers
It may have gone unnoticed with all of the tight ends breaking out, but Freiermuth is averaging 12.1 PPR FPPG and has four touchdowns in five games. He clearly has the trust of Aaron Rodgers and trust usually equates to end zone targets with Rodgers under center. With all the injuries at wide receiver, expect the tight end target share to increase for this offense. Freiermuth is a great replacement option if you are missing Sam LaPorta this week.
FallersJacoby Brissett, QB, Cardinals
Brissett is back to throwing 40 times a game and has seven touchdown passes in his last three games. How can he be a faller? Well, he played the Lions last week and he's facing the Rams this week. That is an enormous difference. I would rather stream Deshaun Watson or Kirk Cousins in Week 6 if you have the option. If you don't, just hope the Cardinals get a couple of garbage-time possessions in the fourth quarter. No one turns those possessions into Fantasy points better than Brissett.RJ Harvey, RB, Broncos
Our only boomerang of the week, and it's a bad one. Harvey was a big riser after seeing 10 targets in Week 4. Sean Payton took over playcalling and Harvey disappeared from the offense. He played just 37% of the snaps and logged his first game of 2026 with zero catches. I don't want to cut him, but understand some will have to. Even in a week with four teams on a bye, Harvey doesn't look like a good flex.Rome Odunze, WR, Bears
Odunze has one game with more than 52 receiving yards, one game with double-digit Fantasy points, and zero touchdowns on the season. While there is optimism about Caleb Williams returning, Odunze only saw a combined seven targets in the two games Williams played to start the year. With all the teams on bye, you may be forced to flex Odunze, but you are doing so based on hope, not any realistic projection.
Harold Fannin, TE, Browns
Fannin had his worst game of the season, which is really saying something considering he has been below 30 receiving yards in three of his five games this season. He looks like the definition of a touchdown or bust tight end, and those were much more appealing in prior years because the position used to be a weak one. Fannin ranks 15th in receptions amongst tight ends and 20th in yards. Maybe he'll score a touchdown but the Browns' implied total of 18.5 doesn't offer a lot of hope in that regard either.Week 6 quarterback projections Week 6 running back projections  Week 6 wide receiver projections  Week 6 tight end projections

title: SEC Power Rankings: Texas A&M keeps sliding entering Week 7 - CBS Sports
description: The Aggies' tumble toward the bottom is picking up steam after they began the season inside the AP top 10
body:
The Aggies' tumble toward the bottom is picking up steam after they began the season inside the AP top 10
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:18 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We're three full weeks into the thick of SEC play, and some very clear tiers are forming. Texas A&M, considered to be in one of the higher tiers prior to the season, is tumbling down the totem pole at an alarming rate.Following a 27-6 loss to Missouri, the Aggies are now 1-3 in SEC play, and all three of those defeats have come by at least 10 points. The last two have come by a combined 50 points.In the wake of Collin Klein's departure, the Texas A&M offense has been inept against the better defenses it's faced. Marcel Reed has taken a step back, and the Aggies rank near the bottom of the league in yards per game (14th) and points per game (12th).This weekend, Texas A&M gets a reprieve as it faces The Citadel, but the back half of the schedule is a gauntlet with road trips to Alabama, South Carolina and Oklahoma. If Mike Elko can't right the ship quickly, it may get worse for the Aggies before it gets better.
As Texas A&M slips further down, here are the updated SEC Power Rankings.
        
            
                CBS Sports 138: Georgia takes top spot over Miami, Notre Dame in college football rankings
                
                    Chip Patterson                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Georgia BulldogsLast week: 3Going into Bryant-Denny Stadium and pulling out a win in primetime is more than good enough to earn the Bulldogs the top spot this week. Gunner Stockton made some big-time throws. The Georgia defense held Keelon Russell in check. Kirby Smart is giving fiery pregame speeches and celebrating with the fans who made the trip to Tuscaloosa. The Dawgs are a football death machine. This is bad news for everyone else.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Alabama Crimson TideLast week: 2Someone had to lose Saturday night's game, and it happened to be Alabama. But nothing about that game made me think the Crimson Tide couldn't get revenge if they got a rematch against the Bulldogs down the line. Kalen DeBoer wasn't thrilled with the officiating in the fourth quarter, and he had every reason to be upset. Ultimately, there isn't much separation between Alabama and Georgia.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Texas LonghornsLast week: 1Texas' offense and special teams showed some warts early, but they didn't come back to bite the Longhorns until Saturday. Oklahoma scored a touchdown on defense (pick-six), and special teams (blocked punt), and a late Arch Manning interception set up a game-winning field goal for the Sooners. The defense is playing too well for the rest of the team to keep putting games in jeopardy every week. Steve Sarkisian has to find some answers -- especially on offense.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Ole Miss RebelsLast week: 6Coming off a disappointing loss in Gainesville, an open date and a game against Vanderbilt were just what the doctor ordered for Ole Miss. The Rebels rolled into Nashville and stomped the Commodores in a game that was never in doubt. Trinidad Chambliss was great, and the run defense looked vastly improved. The latter will be tested this weekend, however, as Missouri travels to Oxford.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Missouri TigersLast week: 7The Tigers have now stomped SEC opponents in two consecutive games. The latest victim was a reeling Texas A&M team, and Missouri ran over, around and through the Aggies to the tune of 252 rushing yards. Jamal Roberts led the way there with 222 yards and two touchdowns on the ground, and he has to be salivating at the idea of facing an Ole Miss defense that has been porous against the run for most of the season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Kentucky WildcatsLast week: 9Look, I'm just as surprised as anyone else. I did not anticipate slotting Kentucky this high at any point this season, but here they are. In past years, I would have expected the Wildcats to blow Saturday night's game against LSU, but they simply out-executed the Tigers down the stretch. That's yet another testament to Will Stein, who has Big Blue Nation dreaming big halfway through the regular season.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. LSU TigersLast week: 4LSU shelled out a lot of money to ... have a worse record through six games than Brian Kelly did at this time last season. Plus, the team's College Football Playoff hopes will depend on running the table, which won't be easy. The Tigers face a feisty Mississippi State team this weekend, and they have a stretch of three games against Alabama, Texas and Tennessee in November. How much weight do those wins over Clemson and Texas A&M carry now? Probably not very much.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Florida GatorsLast week: 5What a difference two weeks can make in college football. Florida went from College Football Playoff hopeful to an SEC also-ran in the blink of an eye. Once the hottest coaching candidate on the market, Buster Faulkner now faces questions about a suddenly ineffective running game. How the Gators respond against Texas in a battle of the wound-lickers will be a good indicator of what to expect the rest of the season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Mississippi State BulldogsLast week: 10Mississippi State jumps out of the frying pan and into the fryer. At least it got a bye week to heal up a little bit. Two weeks after Alabama gave the Bulldogs a dose of reality, they have to visit Death Valley for a game against what will surely be an angry LSU team. If healthy, Kamario Taylor has enough magic to make things interesting, but Mississippi State faces a tall task this weekend.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Oklahoma SoonersLast week: 11Brent Venables whispered it into existence. Oklahoma may have turned its season around with a win over Texas, but maybe it didn't. Don't get me wrong, that was a massive win for the Sooners, but all is not fixed in Norman. Scoring on defense and special teams probably isn't a sustainable strategy for scoring points, and the offense still looked relatively flat in the Red River Rivalry. Having said that, John Mateer protected the football, which was a step in the right direction.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Tennessee VolunteersLast week: 8The Tennessee defense is good enough to keep the team in every game left on its schedule. On the other hand, the Tennessee offense is bad enough to blow every game left on the schedule. If the Volunteers can't sustain drives against the hapless Razorbacks, how are they going to do that against the Crimson Tide?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. South Carolina GamecocksLast week: 15Shane Beamer dumped cold water on his hot seat by going into The Swamp and picking up a three-score win over Florida. LaNorris Sellers looked great! Nyck Harbor made big plays! Dylan Stewart wreaked some havoc on defense! This is why people looked at the Gamecocks as a sneaky-dangerous team prior to the season.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. Auburn TigersLast week: 13Auburn may be destined to remain in this spot all season. The Tigers got an open date last weekend while chaos unfolded around them. Alex Golesh now has to take his team on the road to face Georgia while trying to figure out his offense. Yikes.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. Texas A&M AggiesLast week: 12Maybe I'm just a citizen of the cesspool, but I don't see much to be optimistic about in College Station, at least as far as the rest of this season is concerned. Marcel Reed is completely broken, and the defense is getting steamrolled in conference play. A 1-8 finish in conference play is absolutely on the table right now.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. Vanderbilt CommodoresLast week: 15The Commodores just got blown out by Ole Miss in the pouring rain. The mother of one of the team's quarterbacks was caught on camera referring to the "clowns running this football program." Admittedly, it wasn't a great week in Nashville, so Vanderbilt better get in the win column against Arkansas this weekend.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. Arkansas RazorbacksLast week: 16I really thought about moving the Razorbacks up one spot this week, but I simply couldn't reward Ryan Silverfield for punting with 1:45 remaining in a one-score game at home. Predictably, Tennessee picked up a first down two plays later to ice the game. The Hogs have an opportunity to bounce back in a battle of the SEC punching bags on Saturday.

title: Would the Dodgers actually bench Shohei Ohtani? Struggling superstar faces questions amid 2-0 NLCS hole - CBS Sports
description: After a second half gutted by injuries, Ohtani has proven to be a drain on the disappointing Dodgers so far in th
body:
After a second half gutted by injuries, Ohtani has proven to be a drain on the disappointing Dodgers so far in the NLCS
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:50 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The two-time reigning champion Los Angeles Dodgers have a Shohei Ohtani problem. That seems an absurd thing to say about the two-way phenomenon who's won four MVP awards in the last five seasons, but that's the reality for the Dodgers as they trail the Milwaukee Brewers 2-0 in the best-of-seven National League Championship Series. Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3, when he was pulled from his start against the Padres because of left knee discomfort and soreness in his right biceps. Those injuries kept him out of the All-Star Game and won't allow him to pitch in the postseason. For Ohtani and the Dodgers, though, the current concern is how those injuries are affecting him at the plate. The concern is such that the Dodgers and manager Dave Roberts may be pondering the heretofore unthinkable: benching Ohtani with the season on the line. 
"Yeah, I mean, obviously it hasn't been good," Roberts told reporters following the Dodgers' 7-4 loss to the Brewers in Game 2. "He doesn't feel great. I think for me, it's having a conversation with him tomorrow, kind of try to figure out what's best for him, what's best for us. He certainly has earned that conversation and deserves it. I'll have [that conversation] with him tomorrow."If the Dodgers do decide to sit Ohtani for Wednesday's Game 3, 21-year-old rookie outfielder Josue De Paula would be the likely choice to replace him in the lineup, according to The Athletic. The Dodgers would take such drastic measures, ESPN reports, only if Ohtani is so hindered by those knee and biceps issues that he doesn't feel healthy enough to play. As the Dodgers prepare for what is in essence a must-win Game 3 back in Los Angeles, it's worth exploring this emerging dilemma a bit more closely. Let's do that now with three things to know about the big decision facing Ohtani, Roberts, and the club trying to become the first since the 1998-2000 New York Yankees to win three straight World Series. 
Ohtani has been struggling at the plate for some timeThrough six games and 24 plate appearances this postseason, Ohtani is batting a meager .150/.261/.150 with no extra-base hits and seven strikeouts against three walks. Dipping back into the regular season, Ohtani hasn't homered since Aug. 18. Over that homer-less stretch, which includes a stint on the injured list, and looping in the playoffs, he's batted .156/.283/.200 in his last 107 plate appearances. The underlying worry is that this is more than just a run of bad luck, as Ohtani's quality of contact off the bat has also cratered in recent weeks. Let's take a look at those declines with the date of his last home run, Aug. 17, as the dividing line: Date range/Statistic 				 				 				Avg. exit velocity 				 				 				Hard-hit rate 				 				 				Barrel rate 				 				 				Avg. fly ball distance 				xwOBA 				 				 				Opening Day - Aug. 17 				 				 				93.5 mph 				53.0% 				26.2% 				337.1 ft.370 				Aug. 18 - present 				 				 				91.1 mph 				 				 				47.2% 				 				 				15.1% 				 				 				308.8 ft.270 				Barrel rate is the percentage of balls that leave the bat at the ideal exit velocities and launch angle ranges for power production. Hard-hit rate is the percentage of batted balls that leave the bat at 95 mph or greater, and xwOBA evaluates a hitter's deserved production based on quality and frequency of contact. For context, the MLB average xwOBA this season was .315. As you can see, Ohtani has seen declines, steep in some instances, in all of these measures. These indicators, more so than the usual top-line stats, inform future performance. Therein lies the worry for Ohtani and the Dodgers – that this is much more than just a slump driven by randomness and bad luck. De Paula is a tremendously promising young hitterAs on-the-fly fallback options go, the young De Paula is an excellent one. He entered the 2026 season as one of the top prospects in the game, as De Paula ranked within the top 25 overall by CBS Sports, MLB.com, Baseball Prospectus, and Baseball America. Then during the regular season, he went out and slashed .303/.401/.547 in 124 games for Double-A Tulsa. He did that despite being almost three years younger than his average Texas League peer.That performance earned him a mid-September call-up to Los Angeles, and he thrived across 42 plate appearances with an OPS+ of 198 and elite batted-ball and plate-discipline indicators. Armed with an excellent hit tool and plus power, De Paula, who's retained his rookie eligibility, will enter 2027 as one of the top overall prospects in baseball.  In three trips to the plate this postseason, De Paula has worked a pair of walks, so he's already flashed poise and purpose in such pressure situations. All of that is why the Dodgers may turn to the 21-year-old instead of Ohtani with their season and three-peat hopes in serious peril. The Dodgers are in desperation modeSpeaking of serious peril, the math is as unfriendly toward the Dodgers as you would expect given their current NLCS deficit. In dropping the first two games of the series to Milwaukee, the Dodgers now must win four games before the Brewers win two in order to advance to the World Series. Across the entirety of MLB postseason history, teams down 2-0 in a best-of-seven series have gone on to win that series just 16.8% of the time. It's even worse under the Dodgers' specific circumstances. Teams down 2-0 in a best-of-seven series that opened on the road, as the Dodgers did, have gone on to win the series just 15.6% of the time. By no means are the Dodgers dead, but history is confronting them with strong headwinds at the moment. Desperate times, desperate measures, as the saying goes. And there's no measure so desperate as the prospect of benching the best baseball player in the world.

title: Dan Lanning hints at Oregon QB change as Ducks face must-win vs. Nebraska - CBS Sports

body:
Dylan Raiola, who transferred in from Nebraska, and Brock Thomas will undergo an open QB competition this week if Dante Moore remains sidelined with a concussion
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:13 am ET

            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Oregon Ducks have their backs against the wall after suffering their second loss of the season last Saturday against UCLA, dropping all the way out of the AP poll after starting the year No. 2.After a dismal offensive performance against the Bruins, Dan Lanning's Monday press conference was largely about potential changes on that side of the ball -- both in personnel and staff structure. Lanning admitted that "everything is being evaluated" after the loss to UCLA, but was adamant that he won't reveal anything the Ducks plan on doing differently before they take the field on Saturday against Nebraska. That includes the plan at quarterback should Dante Moore still be unable to go as he works his way back from a concussion suffered against USC. Dylan Raiola, who led Oregon to a win at USC in Moore's place, had a catastrophic performance against UCLA, completing just 6 of 19 passes for 43 yards, throwing a pair of interceptions and losing a fumble. He was pulled in the second half for Brock Thomas, who threw for 149 yards and a touchdown to nearly lead the Ducks to a comeback, only to come up short of tying the game on a controversial two-point conversion attempt. 
Lanning insisted there's still an open competition at quarterback this week if Moore isn't able to play, but noted that's also the case at offensive line and at some defensive spots as well. With regard to the quarterback situation specifically, Lanning did divulge some of his thought process on how they'll determine whether Raiola or Thomas will hit the field on Saturday if Moore cannot start. 
        
            
                Once a national title favorite, Oregon has become college football's biggest disappointment
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"[Saturday's performance] all plays into effect, and the body of work this week all plays into effect. The question was asked of me why not make the change sooner after the game; I think that's fair. On the same note, I think some of the positions we put [Raiola] in weren't successful opportunities as well," Lanning said. "I think we made some adjustments in getting the ball out a little quicker, creating some more open pictures that allowed Brock to do that. "But you have to be able to protect the ball, that's a part of it, and like I said after the game, Dylan's also a guy that played really well against USC and you have to be aware of that too."
Lanning knows this is a delicate situation, and he is understandably trying to protect Raiola because there is a world in which the Ducks need him under center and playing with confidence again at some point this season. That said, noting that the No. 1 job of the quarterback is to protect the football would seem to indicate Thomas has the advantage coming into this week of practice. All of this is moot if Moore is able to return from his concussion, as he was able to do some on-field work on the side coming into last week's game but still has no firm timetable for a return to game action. However, given there aren't any guarantees Moore will be back in time for Saturday's suddenly pivotal game against Nebraska, Lanning and the offensive staff -- which could be getting some restructuring in terms of who is in what role on Saturday -- have to figure out who gives them the best chance of success.On top of that, Lanning admitted there could be a change in who calls the plays on Saturday, but wouldn't reveal any plans beyond that the game-planning effort will be more collaborative. Lanning insisted he still has belief in embattled first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and the rest of his staff, but made it sound like there's the potential for someone else to have the play sheet on Saturday -- he just won't reveal who. 
The play-caller decision can also play a role in the quarterback competition, as a more collaborative game plan will require everyone to be on the same page about which quarterback is taking the snaps and how they fit what they want to do. The additional layer of intrigue here is that Nebraska knows Raiola better than anyone, having had him as the Huskers' starter for the last two seasons. Given Lanning's desire to keep Nebraska challenged on who and what to prepare for, that could play a factor in which quarterback Oregon goes with on Saturday. At 3-2, Lanning seems to recognize that the season is one more loss away from completely unraveling for the Ducks. A three-loss Oregon isn't making it into the College Football Playoff, which means every week from here on out is a must-win situation for the Ducks.

title: Rams vs. Bills thriller: Josh Allen accomplishes something he's never done before in Buffalo's OT win - CBS Sports
description: Buffalo's star QB snapped an 0-7 slump on Monday night

Buffalo's star QB snapped an 0-7 slump on Monday night

        The Buffalo Bills won a potential Super Bowl LXI preview on Monday night, defeating Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams, 37-34, in overtime. It was a remarkable back-and-forth affair that saw both offenses put up 400+ yards of total offense, both teams score touchdowns in the final two minutes, and both clubs make mistakes in overtimeThis matchup proved that Bills quarterback Josh Allen is still one of the best players in the world. He completed 12 of 19 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while adding an incredible 121 yards rushing and another touchdown on the ground. However, the real headline is that Allen accomplished something he had never done before in his career — win in overtime.Previously, Allen was 0-7 in overtime, the worst overtime record by a quarterback in NFL history (including playoffs), according to CBS Sports Research. Josh Allen's record in overtimeDateResult1/4/202022-19 loss at Houston Texans (playoffs)12/12/202133-27 loss at Tampa Bay Buccaneers1/23/202242-36 loss at Kansas City Chiefs (playoffs)11/13/202233-30 loss vs. Minnesota Vikings9/11/202322-16 loss at New York Jets11/26/202337-34 loss at Philadelphia Eagles1/17/202633-30 loss at Denver Broncos (playoffs)10/12/202637-34 win at Los Angeles RamsJosh Allen's production in overtimeFirst seven OT gamesMonday night at RamsW-L0-71-0Team points33Yards per game20.790Turnovers20Allen's first overtime win is definitely one he will remember forever. The Rams won the overtime coin toss and elected to kick since both teams now receive a chance in the extra quarter. It looked like the Bills were well on their way to a touchdown to open overtime, thanks to a 57-yard gain from Khalil Shakir to get Buffalo down to the Rams' 22-yard line. But then James Cook III coughed up the ball for the second time, and it was recovered by Aaron Donald.
The Rams now needed just a field goal to win the game. Stafford and Co. got into the Bills' territory with ease, but then Sean McVay started getting conservative. On a third-and-5 from the Bills' 30-yard line, he called a Kyren Williams run that got stuffed at the line of scrimmage. That set up a 48-yard Harrison Mevis field goal attempt for the win. A 48-yard field goal is definitely makeable, but certainly not a gimme — especially if you're Mevis. He missed a 48-yard field goal outdoors in Philly last week and missed a 50-yard field goal earlier on Monday night. His kick was tipped by the Bills' Greg Rousseau. 
With new life, the Bills marched 35 yards down the field on five plays and set Tyler Bass up with a 45-yard field goal to move the Bills to 4-1, and earn Allen his first-ever overtime victory.

title: USWNT vs. Spain live stream: Where to watch online, start time - CBS Sports
description: Emma Hayes wants her squad to capitalize on its chances after generating 10 shots on target without a goal in Sat
body:
Emma Hayes wants her squad to capitalize on its chances after generating 10 shots on target without a goal in Saturday's 2-0 defeat
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:42 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The United States women's national team will get one more chance to prove they're among the world's best on Tuesday night at Subaru Park.  The group will try to bounce back against Spain and close out the international window after Saturday's 2-0 loss, in which Spain took the lead just 14 minutes in. Despite a flurry of shot creation and attempts on goal, the squad couldn't escape the early hole it dug itself into. The questions facing the team and head coach Emma Hayes are as much about adjustments as they are about finishing in the final third.  Here are three keys to the upcoming game:How to watch USWNT vs. Spain, oddsDate: Tuesday, Oct. 13 | Time: 7 p.m. ETLocation: Subaru Park -- Chester, Pa.TV: TNT | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: USWNT +165; Draw +230; Spain +140Find the finishing touchThe biggest stat Hayes has emphasized following the loss is the team's high totals in shot creation and attempts on target, with nothing to show for it. She's been clear in press conferences that "you can't give them a head start" when discussing the two goals conceded in the first friendly, but the group's response was the highlight despite the lack of goals.  "We have to tighten up on those things because actually, they didn't create a lot of chances, and I think if we defend those moments better, it at least puts us into a stronger position. But I think once you go two nil down against them, then you are faced with chasing the game. And I think probably the first 30 minutes did fine; 30 to 45 minutes, I think we lost our structure. I think the second half it was all about us, but you also have to score to win games," Hayes said in pregame comments.  Despite going down 2-0 early, the squad rallied in attack and finished with 13 shots, 10 on target, and 2.26 expected goals to Spain's 0.43. Hayes sees those numbers as a positive for now.  "But I'm not worried about it. I think this is part of the process. As I said, if I'm here to merely protect a wins record, then I'll pick a lesser opponent. But I'm not here to do that. I'm here to see, well, how much does that gap close with them? And then how far away are we from that, and keep working towards it because they're the best team in the world for a reason," Hayes said. A familiar setting in the midfieldThe last time the USWNT got together was the June window. They played two friendlies against Brazil in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup host nation. It was a taste of what a potential future tournament environment could look like, and they lost the opening match to Brazil 2-1. It's been four months since the group last came together, and some are in the mix for the first time or after long absences.  "We've had one classroom session, and then we trained with the group that hadn't played in any of the minutes. So, as a team, we get our first opportunity now to do those things. I think it's always about doing the same things regardless of result, we've done a game review around the things that we can identify as really clear patterns that we break. Is as it is every game of football, you play the same opponent twice, and there's things within that you can do a bit better," Hayes said of the team's two days since the loss.  As in previous fixtures against top opponents this year, Hayes expects a response from the players in the second game.  "And I think our team has a really good habit of bringing them things into the second game, but we have to do them. Like I say this many times, you can get away with things against weaker opposition. You just can't with [Spain], and so I'll be looking for us to apply that detail to what we're doing, but also know that you don't really have much of a turn turnaround," Hayes said.  Patri Guijarro's opening goal on Saturday showed how quickly Spain turn space into a chance. La Roja recorded only three shots on target but scored twice, so the USWNT cannot afford to be generous around the central areas in front of their back line.  Quick pressure on the first pass into Spain's midfield may help limit their most typical route to goal.
A faster responseAll this is to say that the USWNT wouldn't typically find themselves in a compact shape between the lines, but they were dangerous in transition. That threat can disrupt some of Spain's discipline in their switches and movement with the ball, though it may all be easier said than done when you consider the opponent and timing of the window.  "Some players are coming to the back end of the season. Some are at the beginning of their season. We've been four or five months apart. We're only together nine days. We have two training sessions, one game. I think sometimes we think, 'God, everything must look a certain way. description: Revisiting our list of the top 10 wide receivers in football
body:
Revisiting our list of the top 10 wide receivers in football
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:09 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Before the season started, CBS Sports rolled out its top-10 rankings for players at every position on both offense and defense. Some of those rankings look extremely prescient five weeks into the NFL season. Others do not. That's just the way it goes. Football is an unpredictable game, and even those of us who observe it most closely and get a lot right still get a lot wrong a lot of the time.We're not necessarily here to debate what we got right or wrong, but to revisit our lsit. Because so many wide receivers are off to such great starts this season and delivering jump-off-the-screen performances in big-time games, we wanted to see if there are any updates we can make just under a third of the way through the season.So in the space below, we'll detail the updated top 10. Enjoy.Honorable mentions (in no particular order): Malik Nabers, Tetairoa McMillan, Davante Adams, George Pickens, Garrett Wilson, Parker Washington, DeVonta Smith, Mike Evans, Christian Watson, A.J. Brown10. Zay Flowers, RavensPreseason Rankings: Also receiving votes
Flowers is off to an insane start to the season. He's only played two full games so far (he missed one, left one early and played only 33% of the snaps in another), and he's yet to play a full complement of snaps with Lamar Jackson under center. Yet, he already has 26 catches for 405 yards and a pair of scores. He leads the NFL with 4.45 yards per route run, per Tru Media, and that number was even higher before he had to play a game with his backup quarterback. He's being used by Declan Doyle in a way that maximizes his skill set, and it's beautiful to watch.
9. Chris Olave, SaintsPreseason Rankings: Also receiving votes
Olave is tied for the NFL lead in catches with 39, and he's already got 537 yards (second) as well. He is a target vacuum in the Saints' high-volume passing offense, seeing a look on 26.3% of his routes, according to Tru Media. He's also generated an explosive play (gain of 15+ yards) on 20.4% of his targets, which is the highest mark of his career to date. He's worked more often on the perimeter this season than last (73.2% of his routes compared with 61.0%), but it hasn't stopped him from being a target hog. 8. Drake London, FalconsPreseason Rankings: 9
London is a completely different — and absurdly good — player whenever Michael Penix Jr. is on the field for the Falcons. Penix has played in 17 games, starting 15 of them, over the last three years. In those games, London has caught 100 of 154 passes for 1,535 yards and eight touchdowns. He's seen a target on 33% of his routes and averaged 9.97 yards per target. All of those are elite, best-of-the-best type of numbers. Unfortunately, quarterback play has undermined his performance whenever someone other than Penix has been out there, but that shouldn't take away from what he does when he has solid QB play.7. Nico Collins, TexansPreseason Rankings: 8
Collins is a monster-sized receiver (6-foot-4, 222 pounds) with a monster skill set. Utilized most often as a pure X receiver (he lines up out wide on 88% of his routes, per Tru Media), Collins is tasked with doing the hardest work a receiver can do. He makes it look relatively easy. He's only played in three games this year due to a hamstring injury, but he's gone for 19-249-3 and looked dominant doing it.  
6. Amon-Ra St. Brown, LionsPreseason Rankings: 5
I think it's important to note that while St. Brown often gets labeled as "the best slot receiver" in football, he's actually played more often on the perimeter than on the inside in three straight seasons. He does everything, not just the slot stuff. He's obviously absurdly good in the slot, but he's also really good outside. He's gone for 100-plus catches and 1,100-plus yards in four consecutive seasons, and five 10-plus touchdowns in each of the last three. He's on pace to top all of those numbers again this year. He's the model of consistency.5. CeeDee Lamb, CowboysPreseason Rankings: 6
It's easy to forget what Lamb did the last time he was fully healthy and had Dak Prescott under center for a full season: He led the NFL with 135 catches and piled up 1,749 yards and 12 touchdowns while being named a First Team All-Pro. This season, he's reminding people just how good he is. He's tied with Olave for the league lead in catches, and he also has 507 yards and four touchdowns. Had he not suffered a quad injury during last week's game against Tampa, those numbers would be even better. CeeDee does everything, and he does it all at an extremely high level.4. Justin Jefferson, VikingsPreseason Rankings: 2
Jefferson is another one who has missed some time this year, leaving one game after just seven snaps and missing another with an injury. In his other three games, he has 17 catches for 226 yards and three touchdowns. And one of those games came with a backup quarterback forced into emergency duty, and another came in a driving storm where pass volume was limited. We all know what Jefferson can do when he's healthy and has even adequate QB play. We'll likely see it through the rest of the year.
3. Puka Nacua, RamsPreseason Rankings: 3
Stop me if you've heard this before, but we have another guy who has missed time here. Nacua sat out two games, and yet, after Monday night's 17-catch explosion against the Bills, he already has 31 grabs for 337 yards and a score this season. He led the league at 107.2 yards per game last year, and he's topping that this season at 112.3 per game. He's a physical force as a pass-catcher, run-after-catch guy and a blocker. The only thing keeping him from the top of this list is reliability. He misses too many games and too many plays due to trips to the medical tent. 2. Ja'Marr Chase, BengalsPreseason Rankings: 1
Chase has also missed time this year, leaving one game after just 15 snaps due to a concussion. But he's still at 27-289-4, and he proves every week how much of a freak he is with some of the most ridiculous catches you can imagine. (See his touchdown grabs against the Texans and Dolphins for examples.) He's elite off the line, at the break and after the catch. There's nothing he doesn't do at the highest possible level. He's gone for at least 100-1,200-7 in each of the last three years, and even if he's not on that pace right now, he'll almost surely get there again. It's what he does.1. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, SeahawksPreseason Rankings: 4
JSN leads the NFL with 583 receiving yards, a year after leading the NFL with 1,793 receiving yards. He's gone for 75-plus yards in every game this season and 100-plus in four of five. He's also scored in four of five contests and has an NFL-high seven receiving touchdowns to date. It's impossible to cover him, and right now, he runs the best routes in the league. He wins so easily both off the line and at the break that it's almost hard to fathom how he's not wide the hell open on every single play. (And he usually is, anyway.) This crown will likely be passed back and forth between the top few guys for a while, but right now, JSN has it.
